Learned transformer differential relays are rarely compared on common data, folds and decision logic. We evaluate on simulated 300\,MVA and 40\,MVA plants with trace-grouped cross-validation (3 seeds $\times$ 5 folds, 3,302 traces) and re-implement six published methods at their own sampling rates. Natively, none reaches 93\,\% dependability and 98.8\,\% security together: the two most dependable reach 97.0\,\% and 96.5\,\% at 75.3\,\% and 82.9\,\% security. We then study a dual-path supervisory logic (87T--gated classifier, classifier-alone path, high-set) with interchangeable classifiers. With an equal search and epoch budget, six classifier instances reach 93.5--95.7\,\% dependability and 98.8--99.9\,\% security. A harmonic-restrained 87T tuned on validation traces over an extended grid (post-hoc; 92.8\,\% / 98.9\,\%) cannot be told apart from the deployed LSTM instance of our Simulink closed loop (93.0\,\% / 99.0\,\%; trace-clustered test, $p_{\mathrm{H}}=$\,1.00 on both metrics) and detects more high--impedance faults (69.9\,\% against 65.4\,\%). Four of the six instances are more dependable than this relay, by 1.3--3.0 points (post-hoc, Holm-adjusted), and none is less secure. Transfer to the unseen plant depends on the classifier: zero-shot security is 99.9\,\% with Key's network but 88.4\,\% with the deployed LSTM, whose classifier-alone path caused 87 of 89 false trips; the tuned relay, frozen from plant A, reaches 96.8\,\% / 99.1\,\%. The deployed LSTM relay does not outperform a well--tuned conventional relay; the contribution is the leak--free benchmark, the reproductions and the classifier--agnostic logic.
